# Concave multiplier stationarity gives a base-volume martingale

This note proves an exact finite-dimensional stationarity/transport
equivalence for positive concave sampled multipliers. Its marginals use
actual fiber VOLUMES, unlike the separate physical dual's Jordan SURFACE
marginals. A finite absorbing-chain construction proves the transport
directly from the genuine parameter tangent cone. It does not assume a
stationary flow merely from first moments.

The theorem is explicitly REGULAR SINGLETON for its proper covering groups
and unpenalized in its main active-only form. Section 8 permits additional
atomic deepest bases. Section 6 retains the precise different marginals with
the quadratic penalty. Section 7 gives an actual uniform-fiber lift
obstruction, including a global optimum over the whole concave multiplier
class. None of these results is a proof of OC.

## 1. The actual finite concave parameter cone

Fix a finite lattice-complete base P and positive compatible convex fibers
K_z of total mass M. Write w_z=V_z/M. For every p in P let R_p be the
finite set of extreme points of

    {lambda>=0:sum_z lambda_z=1, sum_z lambda_z z=p}.

The cone of concave sampled arrays is exactly

    C={ell in R^P:ell_p>=sum_z lambda_z ell_z
                       for all p in P,lambda in R_p}.        (1)

Its positive arrays have a continuous concave polyhedral extension to
conv(P): the upper roof max sum lambda_z ell_z over representations of
each real base. The constraints in (1) ensure this roof equals ell_p at
every sampled p. Conversely every concave function's sampled values obey
(1). Thus these are actual concave buffer functions, not independently
adjustable values without a compatible extension.

Fix positive ell in C, geometrically normalized by

    sum_z w_z log ell_z=0.                                (2)

Let T_ell be the exact one-sided tangent cone of C at ell. Since (1) has
finitely many rows,

    h in T_ell iff h_p>=sum lambda_z h_z
        whenever ell_p=sum lambda_z ell_z.                 (3)

Every such h gives ell+t h in C and positive for all sufficiently small
t>=0. Inactive inequalities have a fixed positive slack, so no closure
or limiting qualification is needed. All globally concave sampled h lie
in T_ell. Every affine h and its negative lie there. The directions ell
and -ell also lie there, even if -ell itself is not a concave array.

Geometric normalization of a fixed-body raw motion ell+t h gives

    dot ell_z/ell_z=h_z/ell_z-A_h,
    A_h=sum_z w_z h_z/ell_z.                               (4)

For the positive concave buffer

    f=(ell E/M)^(1/N),       N=d+1,

joint concavity, exact continuous alignment grad_x f=f a_opt, and the
same real convex buffered superlevel sets all persist. If equality is
forced on an anchored combination, strict monotonicity of the weighted
geometric mean also forces equality of ell along that combination. The
hereditary deepest-status/parity theorem is therefore valid for these
concave ell, as recorded in its updated source.

## 2. One separator for physical and multiplier variations

Suppose a genuine joint local minimum of the UNPENALIZED normalized
buffered maximum has a finite regular-singleton covering interface.
Every covering group has a source (p_i,y_i), positive proper coareas,
weights rho_ij summing to one, and

    B_i=sum_j rho_ij/S_ij,
    delta_i=epsilon f_i/B_i>0.                            (5)

Selected groups cover every old maximizing base; the proved contact and
quantile continuation retains the cover and all other-base strict gaps.
Supporting caps in other fibers are excluded from this linear statement
unless the full parameters are differentiable there. No density argument
is used to assume this regular setting at a general minimum.

For a parameter-only h in T_ell the actual covering raw-mass derivative is

    q_i'(h)=delta_i/N [h_(p_i)/ell_(p_i)-A_h].             (6)

Take any physically addable cone of actual signed body speeds, for example
the signed complete-global-cut cone. Combine each body speed with any h
in (3), followed by geometric normalization using the NEW body masses.
These are actual competitors. Their finite response vectors form a convex
cone. A vector making all covering derivatives negative is impossible at
the local minimum. Finite separation therefore gives ONE eta_i>=0,
sum eta_i=1, which tests both the body directions and (6), so

    sum_i eta_i q_i'(h)>=0 for EVERY h in T_ell.           (7)

The same eta remains in the physical response dual; it is not replaced
by an unrelated parameter-only separator. No closedness of the response
cone is needed for separation from the open strict-improvement orthant.

Set Delta=sum_i eta_i delta_i>0 and define finite BASE measures

    mu=sum_i eta_i delta_i/ell_(p_i) delta_(p_i),
    nu=Delta sum_z w_z/ell_z delta_z.                     (8)

Then (7) is exactly

    <mu-nu,h>>=0 for all h in T_ell.                      (9)

These are actual inverse-ell tilted VOLUME weights. Nu is positive at
EVERY sampled base. Mu is supported on the positively weighted covering
sources. Equations (8) alone do not give equal mass or first moment;
those equalities follow from the two-sided affine tests in (9).

## 3. Exact equivalence with an ell-tight martingale

For the measures (8), the following are equivalent:

* the full tangent inequality (9);
* mu and nu have equal mass and first base moment, mu is dominated by nu
  in convex order, and their integrals of ell are equal;
* there is a nonnegative matrix pi_(pz) whose source marginal is mu,
  target marginal is nu, and whose every positive source row satisfies

      sum_z pi_(pz) z=mu_p p,
      sum_z pi_(pz) ell_z=mu_p ell_p.                     (10)

Convex order means integral phi dmu<=integral phi dnu for every finite
convex function of the REAL base. The linear marginal/mean equations and
pi>=0 are a precise finite linear feasibility problem. They involve no
continuous fiber coordinates.

Here is a direct proof and construction. The dual of the finite cone (3)
gives, by finite Farkas separation,

    mu-nu=sum_e tau_e(e_(p_e)-lambda_e),   tau_e>=0,       (11)

where every e is an ell-TIGHT extreme anchored representation in (1).
This identity is supplied by the actual tangent stationarity. It is not
an assumed flow balance. Let out_p=sum_(e:p_e=p)tau_e and
in_p=sum_e tau_e lambda_(e,p). Then (11) says

    mu_p+in_p=nu_p+out_p=:m_p>0.                         (12)

At each p start with injected mass mu_p. At each visit stop with
probability nu_p/m_p; otherwise move by the outgoing transition weights
sum_(e:p_e=p)tau_e lambda_(e,z)/m_p. Because P is finite and every nu_p>0,
the stopping probabilities have a strictly positive common lower bound.
Thus all injected mass stops almost surely with finite expected visit
count; isolated loops or closed nonabsorbing classes cannot occur.

The proposed total visit masses m_p solve the injected flow equation
by (12). This solution is unique because the transition matrix is
strictly substochastic in the preceding uniform sense. Consequently
the actual final absorbed marginal is exactly nu. Each step preserves
the conditional mean of the base, since lambda_e is anchored, and of
ell, since that representation is tight. The bounded stopped processes
therefore preserve both conditional means through absorption. Their
source-to-final coupling is pi in (10).

Such a martingale proves convex order by conditional Jensen. Conversely
convex order plus equality of the ell integrals proves (9): for h in
T_ell, ell+t h is actually concave for small positive t. Its concave
test inequality, after subtracting the equal ell integrals, is exactly
t<mu-nu,h>>=0. Finite concave roofs realize these tests. This also proves
that (9) is an exact stationarity reformulation, not an extra inequality
independent of the same parameter freedoms.

The equality of ell moments is automatic for the particular marginal
formulas in (8): both equal Delta. It is listed in the equivalence to
make the Jensen/contact content and converse explicit.

## 4. What the base contact statement actually says

Disintegrate any such martingale at a source p. Concavity gives

    ell_p>=sum_z lambda_z ell_z,
    lambda_z=pi_(pz)/mu_p,

and (10) makes it equality. For any affine supergradient plane of the
concave roof at p, all positively weighted targets lie on the SAME
ell-contact plane. Finite polyhedral support planes exist at boundary
bases as well. Conversely equality for the chosen target row is the
exact ell-affinity condition.

The bases and original fibers are real, so each conditional row is an
actual anchored relation with the genuine inclusion

    sum_z lambda_z K_z subset K_p.                       (13)

However (10) does not make (13) an equality, align the fiber centroids
or selected continuous marks, or give a boundary-contact normal. This
ell contact is different from the physical-support contact of the
separate SURFACE Jordan martingale. The two couplings have different
marginals and cannot be substituted for one another.

One useful conditional rigidity is exact. If at an active source p every
nontrivial anchored representation has STRICT ell Jensen inequality,
then its row of pi must be the identity row. If this holds at every
positive mu source, pi is entirely the identity. Since nu is positive
on all P, every base then belongs to the positive source support and

    sum_(i:p_i=p) eta_i delta_i=Delta w_p                 (14)

at every base. No claim that such strict sampled concavity occurs at a
joint minimum is made; globally affine ell makes every anchored relation
tight and does not yield this rigidity.

A simpler extremal-base consequence needs no strict ell inequality.
If every positive mu source is a vertex of conv(P), each martingale row
is necessarily the identity, because an extreme base has no nontrivial
anchored representation. Positivity of nu then forces EVERY sampled
base to be one of these sources and a vertex. Lattice completeness makes
their parities distinct: two equal-parity distinct vertices would have
their integer midpoint in P, a nonvertex. Thus k(P)=|P|, and the centroid
of a largest fiber already has ordinary depth at least
Gamma_d max V_z>=Gamma_d M/k(P). Therefore in the unpenalized regular
all-proper BELOW-TARGET setting, some positively weighted source must be
a nonvertex of the base polytope. This is a parameter-transport consequence,
not a proof of independent physical freedom at that nonvertex fiber.

At an ell-contact face, there are additional finite concave test
inequalities such as integral log ell dmu>=integral log ell dnu. These
are consequences of the same transport, not automatic equalities. In
particular ell-affinity of a row does not mean ell is constant on it.

## 5. Strongest scope currently justified

The certificate is a real gain over mere tilted-barycenter containment:
all convex base tests and an exact ell-contact decomposition are retained,
with the FULL positive inverse-ell volume target. It remains equivalent
to the complete parameter tangent stationarity and leaves the actual
continuous-coordinate coupling unresolved.

The same derivation applies whenever the established continuation gives
the linear responses (6) and a physically convex joint response cone.
The general nonsmooth supporting inverse is nonlinear, and a general
multiple-contact response takes a minimum. Neither is linearized here.
In particular no nonregular finite-menu theorem is asserted merely from
the existence of a concave parameter family.

## 6. Exact penalty version: the source is no longer active-only

If the objective is instead beta+epsilon^2(P_ar-1), where
P_ar=sum_z w_z ell_z, retain the actual penalty derivative

    P_ar'(h)=sum_z w_z h_z-P_ar sum_z w_z h_z/ell_z.

The SAME joint separator now yields (9) and all its conclusions for

    mu_pen=mu+NM epsilon^2 sum_z w_z delta_z,
    nu_pen=(Delta+NM epsilon^2 P_ar)
                              sum_z w_z/ell_z delta_z.     (15)

Both are positive measures, and their ell integrals agree exactly.
The finite stopping construction still works because nu_pen is positive
on all P. But the source has an additional full-volume component.
Removing this component, or asserting the active-only coupling (8) for
the penalized objective, is unjustified. No penalty-relative-smallness
assumption is introduced.

## 7. Actual optimum over all concave ell, and no uniform-fiber lift

Use Two-sided's certified actual family

    P={-1,0,1},  K_-=K_+=[-1,1],  K_0=[-1,2],
    (V_-,V_0,V_+)=(2,3,2),  M=7, Sigma=43/84.            (16)

It has strict proper closed-minor quotas and nonaffine continuous centroid
graph (0,1/2,0). The full all-normal calculation is in
`candidate 14357e41460c996b`.
Endpoint bases have buffered depth at most 2 for EVERY multiplier, while
the middle already has ordinary depth 13/4. Its buffered depth depends
only on ell_0 and increases strictly above its value at ell_0=1 for
0<epsilon<=10^(-4). The unique middle maximizing mark at ell_0=1 is

    y_epsilon=1/4+delta_epsilon/2>1/4,
    Q_epsilon=13/4+3delta_epsilon/2,                      (17)

where delta_epsilon is the positive root

    (1+t)delta^2-t delta-35t/4=0,
    t=43epsilon^2/1764.                                  (18)

There is a regular selected menu; the all-direction proof is retained
from that source, not inferred by checking selected caps alone.

The multiplier minimum is still unique at ell=1 in the enlarged cone
of ALL positive concave sampled arrays. Indeed concavity and (2) give

    0=(2/7)log ell_-+(3/7)log ell_0+(2/7)log ell_+
      <=(4/7)log[(ell_-+ell_+)/2]+(3/7)log ell_0
      <=log ell_0.

Thus ell_0>=1. Equality forces ell_-=ell_0=ell_+=1. Every other positive
concave normalized array has ell_0>1 and strictly increases the middle
maximum. Endpoints never compete, so this is an exact GLOBAL parameter
optimum, not just affine or formal stationarity. It is not a claimed
joint minimum over body deformations.

Here the normalized base martingale is exactly

    delta_0  -->  (2 delta_-1+3 delta_0+2 delta_1)/7.      (19)

It satisfies all concave tangent tests by Jensen, with ell contact
trivially everywhere. However the continuous mean of the full target
mixture with UNIFORM conditional distributions on the actual fibers is

    [2*0+3*(1/2)+2*0]/7=3/14<1/4<y_epsilon.             (20)

No joint transport with those target marginals can have source continuous
mean y_epsilon. This rules out a silent uniform-fiber lift of (19), even
at the unique optimum over the full concave multiplier cone with actual
regular caps and strict quotas. It does not rule out a different,
geometrically justified choice of conditional target distributions.
The example is safely above the mixed target, and does not refute OC.

## 8. Mixed atomic/proper maxima: the active-only target survives

the contributor's following extension removes the all-proper requirement in the
unpenalized below-target regime. Let I be the full deepest base set,
J={p in I:b_base(p)>Q}, and A=I\J. The hereditary/parity theorem, now
valid for positive concave ell, supplies m_A closed pure-base mass-Q
caps G_s covering A and excluding J, with

    m_A+k(J)<=k(I).                                      (21)

Assume the proper bases J admit the finite REGULAR SINGLETON covering
groups used above. Include the atomic G_s as additional covering rows.
For a signed actual body speed v, their normalized improvement is simply

    R_s^atomic(v)=D_(G_s)-beta D,
    D_(G_s)=sum_(z in G_s) integral_(boundary K_z) v_z,   (22)

and their multiplier-only derivative is zero. This is an exact physical
response of a fixed closed pure-base cap; it has no coarea, energy, or
covariance correction. These atomic rows and the proper rows cover all
old deepest bases, and off-I gaps persist under the same actual path.

Take ONE separator over the combined proper/atomic response cone. It
cannot put all its weight on atomic rows when beta m_A<1. Indeed the
root convex-base-hinge construction produces ONE actual compatible speed
array with total first loss D=m_A and EVERY atomic captured first loss
at least 1. It belongs to the signed complete-global-cut cone (its field
is a nonnegative convex function of the base alone). Consequently an
atomic-only separator would evaluate its improvement at least

    1-beta m_A>0,

contradicting the separator inequality. If m_A=0 there are no atomic
weights to consider. Thus

    Delta=sum_(i proper) eta_i delta_i>0.                 (23)

In particular beta<1/k(P) implies the needed inequality by (21). The
mixed below-target condition beta<Gamma_d/k(P) is stronger. If J were
empty, the same hinge action excludes the minimum outright, as in the
audited purely atomic theorem.

Parameter variations have zero response in the atomic rows. Therefore
Sections 2–4 apply UNCHANGED with mu supported only on the positive proper
group sources, Delta as in (23), and

    nu=Delta sum_(ALL z in P) w_z/ell_z delta_z.           (24)

The same common eta continues to test the whole physical cone. In its
unpenalized physical density, only the cap selector changes:

    W_z(X)=sum_(proper i,j) eta_i theta_ij kappa_ij(z,X)
                    +sum_(atomic s) eta_s 1_(z in G_s).

All source-energy and covariance terms have their previous coefficients
with delta present only for proper groups; Delta is (23), and the common
mass term remains -beta because ALL eta, including atomic eta, sum to one.
The logarithmic normalization term is -Delta log ell_z/(NM). No part of
the original fiber mass is discarded from the target (24).

This extension neither linearizes nonregular proper rows nor deletes
the penalty. With a penalty the hinge test has its additional arithmetic
normalization cost, so (23) does not follow from the same argument alone.
When that objective is used, Section 6's different marginals must be kept.

The vertex-source consequence in Section 4 consequently applies also
with atomic deepest bases present: at an unpenalized regular-proper bad
minimum, some POSITIVELY WEIGHTED proper source is a nonvertex of conv(P).
Atomic bases do not secretly supply the source injection of (24).

## 9. Verification

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_concave_multiplier_volume_martingale_defect_transport.py` passes
3,152 exact symbolic/rational checks, including reciprocal transition
cycles with exact all-stopping marginals, a nonaffine ell-contact roof,
the penalized equations, and the enlarged concave-array calibration.
The inherited actual interval verifier passes 4,810 additional exact checks.
The finite tangent/transport and actual response arguments above are
analytic proofs, not assertions of actual criticality for generated flow
arrays in the checker.
